label: thm:ftc1
title: First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement: Let $f$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and set $F(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$. Then $F'(x) = f(x)$ for every interior point $x$.
proof: We apply \texttt{integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}. The three hypotheses are: integrability on sub-intervals (Lemma~\ref{lem:interval_integrable_restriction}), strong measurability at the point (Lemma~\ref{lem:strongly_measurable_interior}), and continuity at the point (Lemma~\ref{lem:continuous_at_interior}).
